_comment: Vocabulary for the ASR translation guard (backend/english_transcript.py).
This is data, not code, for the same reason the report clean-up patterns
are: which number words a dictation uses, and which clinical opposites
matter, are properties of the language and specialty being dictated -- not
of the verification algorithm. A site dictating in a different language, or
a modality with its own polarity pairs, edits this file and changes nothing
Both tables are safety-relevant. Read the notes before editing either.

_why: A faithful translation renders a spoken number as a digit, so comparing
digits alone marks a CORRECT rendering of 'سی' as '30' an invented
number and rejects it. Every word here is a value the output may
OMISSIONS ARE DELIBERATE. 'نه' (nine) is absent because in clinical
dictation it is overwhelmingly the negation 'no' ('نه با سکولاریتی' =
'no vascularity'). Admitting it would let a genuinely fabricated 9 pass
unnoticed. Prefer excluding an ambiguous word: the cost is a false
rejection that the repair pass resolves, versus a fabrication served as
Clinical opposites a translation must not flip. The numeral check cannot
see an inverted term, and an inverted one reads as a perfectly normal
finding. Observed on real dictation: source 'هایپوکوک' (HYPOechoic)
returned as 'hyperechoic' -- one syllable, opposite meaning, and nothing
Each entry is [low_pole_term, high_pole_term]. A conflict is only raised
when the source carries one pole unambiguously and the output carries
only the other, so a fragment discussing both is left alone.
_source_hints: Substrings that reveal which pole the SOURCE carries, before translation
has happened. Includes the Persian transliterations these arrive as.
